```
springBoot {

```

Maven Changes
Users that build their Spring Boot project with Maven should review the following section.

Running Your Application in the Maven Process
The `fork` attribute of `spring-boot:run` and `spring-boot:start` that was deprecated in Spring Boot 2.7 has been removed.

### Dependency Management Changes

The following changes have been made to dependencies managed by Spring Boot.

#### JSON-B

Dependency management for Apache Johnzon has been removed in favor of Eclipse Yasson.
A Jakarta EE 10-compatible version of Apache Johnzon can be used with Spring Boot 3, but you will now have to specify a version in your dependency declaration.

#### ANTLR 2

Dependency management for ANTLR 2 (`antlr:antlr`) has been removed as it was no longer required.
If you are using ANTLR 2 in your application, specify a version that meets your needs.

#### RxJava

Dependency management for RxJava 1.x and 2.x has been removed and dependency management for RxJava 3 has been added in its place.

#### Hazelcast Hibernate Removed

skill_drafts.name: Spring Boot 3 Dependency Management Migration
skill_drafts.description: Identify and update removed or replaced dependency management entries when upgrading from Spring Boot 2.7 to 3.0. Ensures explicit version declarations for affected libraries: Apache Johnzon (JSON-B), ANTLR 2, RxJava (1.x/2.x → 3.x), and Hazelcast Hibernate.
applicable_signals: Spring Boot version in pom.xml or build.gradle is 2.7.x
Project uses Apache Johnzon, ANTLR 2, RxJava 1.x/2.x, or Hazelcast Hibernate
Build fails with missing or conflicting dependency versions
contraindications: Already on Spring Boot 3.0 or later
Project does not use any of the affected libraries
No dependency management changes are required
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Locate dependency management section', 'detail': 'Open pom.xml (Maven) or build.gradle (Gradle) and find the dependencyManagement or plugins block'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Check for JSON-B (Apache Johnzon)', 'detail': 'If Apache Johnzon is present, replace with Eclipse Yasson or add explicit version for Jakarta EE 10-compatible Johnzon'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Check for ANTLR 2', 'detail': 'If antlr:antlr is declared, add explicit version matching your application needs'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Check for RxJava 1.x or 2.x', 'detail': 'Replace RxJava 1.x or 2.x with RxJava 3 and add explicit version declaration'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Check for Hazelcast Hibernate', 'detail': 'If Hazelcast Hibernate is present, add explicit version or remove if no longer needed'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Verify build', 'detail': 'Run mvn clean install or gradle build to confirm all dependencies resolve without errors'}
triggers: Upgrading Spring Boot project from 2.7.x to 3.0
Reviewing pom.xml or build.gradle for managed dependencies
Dependency resolution errors after Spring Boot 3.0 upgrade
constraints: Must review all managed dependencies in the build configuration
Explicit version declarations must be added for each removed or replaced library
Build must succeed without dependency resolution errors after changes
cautions: Do not remove dependency declarations without verifying that your application does not use the library
Ensure version compatibility between upgraded libraries and other project dependencies
Test transitive dependency resolution to avoid runtime classpath conflicts
output_contract: Updated pom.xml or build.gradle with explicit version declarations for all affected libraries (Apache Johnzon, ANTLR 2, RxJava 3, Hazelcast Hibernate); build succeeds without dependency resolution errors; project is ready for Spring Boot 3.0 upgrade

metadata.prompt: Review your pom.xml or build.gradle for managed dependencies that have been removed or replaced in Spring Boot 3.0. For each affected library, add explicit version declarations to your dependency block. Verify that the build resolves all transitive dependencies without conflicts.

skill_drafts.name: Maven Build Configuration Update for Spring Boot 3
skill_drafts.description: Remove the deprecated `fork` attribute from `spring-boot:run` and `spring-boot:start` Maven plugin goals, and configure Gradle Kotlin DSL `buildInfo` exclusions as needed for Spring Boot 3.0 compatibility.
applicable_signals: pom.xml contains <fork>true</fork> or <fork>false</fork> in spring-boot-maven-plugin configuration
Gradle build.gradle.kts uses buildInfo block without excludes configuration
Maven or Gradle build targets Spring Boot 3.0 or later
contraindications: Already using Spring Boot 3.0 or later without fork attribute
Gradle build does not use buildInfo exclusions
Build configuration is not Maven or Gradle
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Open pom.xml and locate spring-boot-maven-plugin configuration', 'check': 'Plugin block is found and readable'}

{'step': 2, 'action': 'Remove <fork>true</fork> or <fork>false</fork> from spring-boot:run and spring-boot:start goal configurations', 'check': 'No fork attribute remains in the plugin configuration'}

{'step': 3, 'action': 'For Gradle projects, open build.gradle.kts and add or update springBoot { buildInfo { excludes.set(setOf(...)) } } block', 'check': 'buildInfo block is syntactically valid and excludes are specified'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Run mvn clean build or gradle build to validate configuration', 'check': 'Build completes without deprecation warnings related to fork attribute'}
triggers: Migrating Maven or Gradle build configuration to Spring Boot 3.0
`fork` attribute present in spring-boot:run or spring-boot:start goals
Build log shows deprecation warnings for fork attribute
constraints: fork attribute removal applies only to Maven spring-boot-maven-plugin
buildInfo exclusions apply only to Gradle Kotlin DSL projects
Changes must be made before running the build
cautions: Removing fork attribute may change process isolation behavior; test application startup in the Maven process
Verify that excluded properties (e.g., 'time') are not required by downstream build steps or runtime configuration
output_contract: pom.xml or build.gradle.kts is updated with fork attribute removed and buildInfo exclusions configured as needed; Maven or Gradle build executes successfully without deprecation warnings; application starts in the Maven process without errors.

metadata.prompt:
1. Locate `spring-boot:run` and `spring-boot:start` plugin goal configurations in pom.xml.
2. Remove any `fork` attribute declarations (deprecated in Spring Boot 2.7, removed in 3.0).
3. For Gradle projects using Kotlin DSL, add or update the `springBoot { buildInfo { excludes.set(...) } }` block to exclude properties such as 'time' if needed.
4. Verify the build configuration file syntax is valid.
5. Run a test build to confirm no deprecation warnings are emitted.
